Solid and Svelte join React and Vue with one kit under the same names in all four, and twenty new components bring their words in all 42 languages of the glossary.

**Adopting apps:**

- **Moving up:** install `@glimstone/core` with `@glimstone/react`, `@glimstone/vue`, `@glimstone/solid` or `@glimstone/svelte` at 4.5.0, all four packages at the same number.
- **Deprecated names:** `Badge`'s `shape`, `BadgeShape`, `AboutCard`, `DropdownListbox` and the Vue `ToastViewport` listeners `enter`, `leave`, `focusin` and `focusout` keep working until 5.0.0. Each one says so once on the console with what to use instead. `npx glimstone-migrate src` rewrites what it can in place and names file and line for the rest, and `--check` fails a CI step while anything is left.
- **Vue toasts and giving windows:** `ToastViewport` emits `mouse-enter`, `mouse-leave`, `focus` and `blur`, the names of React's handlers. `CryptoDonateDialog` takes its QR code and coin marks in the `qr` and `mark` slots, `PaypalDialog` takes its selector in `selector` and binds `frequency`, `preset` and `typed` with `v-model`.
- **Types:** `CryptoCoin`, `CryptoNetwork`, `ToastViewportEntry`, `SidebarCount`, `InstanceFigure`, `SignInLabelKeys`, `FortressLabelKeys` and `MenuBarHandle` live in `@glimstone/core`. React re-exports them under the same names, so an import from `@glimstone/react` keeps working.
- **Your own copy of the tokens:** take the colour block whole, since each theme is written once with `light-dark()`. `--ink-mix` is still set but deprecated, and `glimstone-migrate` moves your CSS onto `--accent-ink` and `--item-hue-glyph`. Take the `--focus-ring`, `--accent-hover` and `.glim-list-filter` lines too, and point your own `::placeholder` rules at `--field-placeholder`. Every component rule sits in `@layer components`, so check any unlayered rule of yours that counted on losing to GlimStone. A rule that keyed off `[data-motion='subtle']` to find the quiet level should test for `wild` instead.
- **Copies that drift:** `npx glimstone-drift src` compares an app's copied files with the release its `GLIMSTONE_VERSION` names and lists each one that differs, plus `glim-` classes of the app's own and deprecated names still in use. `--strict` fails CI on any of them.
- **The fortress after a removal:** once a member is removed, the kit lets no new app join until the phrase changes, and the old phrase gets nobody in. `removeBack`, `removedBody` and `removedNote` say exactly that, and `removedHereHint` points the removed app to the new phrase. The kit refuses a join in that window with the code `closedUntilNewPhrase`. Let `onJoin` answer `{ code }` and `Fortress` shows `joinLocked`, the way `phrase` shows `joinRefused`. An `error` of the app's own still wins, and `joinRefusalText(text, code)` gives the same sentence for a window of the app's own.
- **Plugin pages:** every release carries `glimstone-plugin-4.5.0.zip` for a page without a build step, with the core as `glimstone.js` on `window.GlimStone` and as `glimstone.mjs`, plus `tokens.css`, the fortress card and `glyphs.json`. A plugin that copies `packages/core/vanilla/fortress-card.js` takes it again: it carries the fortress's new words in every language and shows `joinLocked` when the adapter's `join` rejects with `{ code: "closedUntilNewPhrase" }`.
- **Flutter:** move the git dependency to `ref: v4.5.0`. The package needs Flutter 3.27 or later. `GlimTheme` takes `inkLightness` and the new `fieldPlaceholder`, and the focus ring comes from a getter on `GlimDerived`. `inkMix` and the `focusRing` argument still compile as deprecated until 5.0.0, and `glimstone-migrate` rewrites them in your Dart files.
- **Version:** `GLIMSTONE_VERSION` from `@glimstone/core` reads 4.5.0.

## ✨ Added

- **`@glimstone/solid` and `@glimstone/svelte`** carry every component under React's names, props and defaults and draw the same markup, so an app keeps its look in any of the four. Solid takes controlled values with `onChange`. Svelte 5 adds `bind:value` and `bind:checked` beside the callbacks and takes snippets for markup.
- **React and Vue are twins.** Every component, hook and type has a namesake in the other package with the same props, defaults, events and markup, so an app can switch frameworks by changing its imports. A parity test fails the moment the packages drift apart, and every demo is compared element by element across all four.
- **Twenty new components** on Zag's machines: `Accordion`, `Collapsible`, `Avatar`, `Pagination`, `PinInput`, `TagsInput`, `Steps`, `Splitter`, `ScrollArea`, `FileUpload`, `DatePicker`, `Rating`, `Timer`, `AngleSlider`, `SignaturePad`, `HoverCard`, `Carousel`, `Marquee`, `Tour` and `FloatingPanel`. They follow the APG keyboard patterns where one exists, and the ones that move stop or land at once at the motion level off and under reduced motion.
- **One token source in the DTCG format.** Style Dictionary writes `tokens.css`, `tailwind-theme.css`, `tokens.g.dart` and `figma-variables.json` from `packages/core/tokens`, and CI fails when one of them differs. A tool that reads W3C design tokens can take `@glimstone/core/tokens/*.json`, and `figma-variables.json` sets up the colours, shapes, densities and lengths as Figma variables.
- **Row density.** `data-density` is `compact`, `normal` or `airy`, for rows 32, 42 or 52px tall. `applyDensity()` sets it, `cacheAppearance()` keeps it, and every package has `useDensity()`. Normal matches the rows apps already have.
- **Spacing and elevation scales.** `--space-1` to `--space-13` run from 2 to 40px, and every padding, margin and gap in the components reads a step. `--elevation-raised`, `--elevation-float` and `--elevation-modal` are the three shadows, with `--z-raised` up to `--z-bubble` as the stacking order that goes with them.
- **A contrast step.** Under `prefers-contrast: more`, or with `data-contrast="more"` on the root, the accent's ink, the muted text, the borders and the focus ring all step up, and cards, fields and buttons get an edge. An app that draws its own rings reads the new `--focus-ring-width`.
- **Windows contrast themes.** Under `forced-colors: active` every card, field, button and badge gets an edge in the system's text colour, and a chosen or switched-on control takes the system's selection colours.
- **Chart colours.** Eight series, a sequential blue and a diverging blue to orange, all OKLCH and in every theme. Any two series stay apart under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia, and Flutter gets them on `GlimTheme`.
- **`fromEnd` on `ContextMenu`** opens a menu with the focus on its last row, for an app's own menu bar. The brand marks gain `REACT_SVG`, `VUE_SVG`, `SOLID_SVG`, `SVELTE_SVG` and `FLUTTER_SVG`.
- **`joinLocked`** tells an app that tries to join after a removal, before the phrase has changed, why the fortress turns it away and that it needs the new phrase. React, Vue, Solid, Svelte and the plugin card pick it for the kit's code on their own, so an app only passes the code on.
- **The site shows the kit at work.** The start page leans a slowly drifting wall of screens built from the real components beside its heading. Make it yours opens the look controls in a panel laid out like an app's settings page, with a snippet to copy. Blocks offers whole page parts such as a sign-in page, a settings page and a list page with its empty states, live in all four frameworks with their code.

## 🎨 Design

- **The accent ramps are built in OKLab.** The eight presets read between 5.2 and 5.9:1 as text on white, and the light theme's fault and warning washes are lighter, so their text reaches 4.5:1.
- **Each theme is written once** with `light-dark()`, and a chosen theme wins over the system in both directions, on a subtree too.
- **A page without a setting gets soft corners and calm motion**, the same defaults `appearance.ts` gives.
- **Components answer to their own width.** A field row wraps its controls, a list row hides its badges and an instance card takes the smaller mark when their own width runs short, wherever they stand.
- **Deprecation follows a fixed rule.** A name gets one console warning and leaves in the next major.
- **Each rule says what holds and why**, and how it came about lives in `docs/decisions.md`. The site's Rules page is built from the design language, and a test fails when anything cites a rule that does not exist.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The keyboard follows the APG in more places.** Home and End open a closed `Select` on its first or last option, Space flips a `Checkbox` as on a native one, a letter jumps to its row in menus and in `DropdownListbox`, PageUp and PageDown move ten rows in a `ListTable`, and Tab stays inside an open `Sheet`.
- **Every target on the demo pages is at least 24 pixels**, as WCAG 2.2 asks.
- **A plain rule of the app's own wins** over GlimStone's components, since they sit in `@layer components`.
- **A removal closes the fortress to new apps until the phrase changes.** The remove window, the question after it and the line under the switch say so plainly, where they used to promise the old phrase a way back in. An app that was removed learns that the new phrase brings it back once the phrase has changed.
- **Tests run wider.** Every contract row runs once per framework, the site is tested in Firefox as well, with screenshots and an axe check, and CI fails when a stylesheet or bundle grows past its size budget.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The focus ring is opaque and reaches 3:1** on every ground it stands on, in every theme, for every preset and any picked colour.
- **Placeholder text reaches 4.5:1** on every field fill.
- **A picked mid-tone accent keeps its ink readable under the pointer.** Where a hover would take the ink under 4.5:1, `applyAccent()` steps it the other way, and Flutter's `GlimTheme.withAccent()` follows the same rules.
- **A reactive button stays under the pointer.** It keeps the width its label takes in the other modes, so a wrapping row can't slide it away and back without end.
- **The README pictures look their scenes up in a `Map`**, so a link with `?scene=constructor` or `?scene=toString` can't break the stage page.
- **The overlay test reads its dials with a real whitespace class**, where `\s` inside a template literal reached `RegExp` as a plain `s`.

## 🌐 Translations

- **The twenty new components speak all 42 languages** of the glossary, plural forms and digits included. `componentText(lang)` hands out the words, each language is a module of its own under `componentLocales/`, and an app's own words win over them.
- **The fortress's new words are in all 42 languages too**, each in its own terms and form of address.
